outcome: Currently meeting the criteria for metabolic syndrome (3 or more of: large waist, high triglycerides, low HDL, high blood pressure or BP medicine, high fasting glucose or diabetes / diabetes medicine)

criteria.label: Large waist
criteria.rule: Waist ≥ 102 cm (40 in) for men, ≥ 88 cm (35 in) for women

criteria.label: High triglycerides
criteria.rule: Triglycerides ≥ 150 mg/dL, or on medicine for high triglycerides

criteria.label: Low HDL (“good”) cholesterol
criteria.rule: HDL < 40 mg/dL for men, < 50 mg/dL for women, or on medicine for low HDL

criteria.label: High blood pressure
criteria.rule: Blood pressure ≥ 130/85 mmHg, or on blood-pressure medicine

criteria.label: High fasting blood sugar
criteria.rule: Fasting glucose ≥ 100 mg/dL, or diagnosed diabetes / on glucose-lowering medicine

survey_adjustment.note: Survey-cycle term fixed to 2017-2020 (RECENT = 1) and folded into the intercept.

training.source: NHANES 2011-2012 + 2017-March 2020, rebuilt from the CDC files (ml/nhanes.py)
training.label: ATP III / harmonized, medicines included (BP medicine; diagnosed diabetes, insulin or diabetes pills)
training.v1_label_finding: The v1 training file (metabolic_syndrome.csv) was matched to the CDC 2011-12 files by participant ID: every value is identical, and its label matches the measured-values-only definition (no medicines) for 97.5% of people. v2 uses one definition, with medicines, for both surveys.

validation.scheme: 5-fold x 5-repeat stratified cross-validation, both surveys pooled

odds_ratios.unit: men vs women, age 50, waist 98 cm

history.note: Trained on the 2011-12 extract (label without medicines); CV AUC 0.833.
v1 + intercept shift (+0.24) after external validation on NHANES 2017-2020 (AUC 0.844, O/E 1.10 -> 1.00).
Retrained on both surveys with one label definition (medicines included).
